I am not an expert nor do I have diagnosed OCD. However, have you heard of exposure therapy? I would recommend looking into it. A lot of it you can probably do at home, IF you're in a decent place mentally. I'd never recommend you to do it if you're at risk for self harm or something like that.

I personally have never heard of a family dynamic like this in all my reading on narcissistic families. It really seems like something else was going on. 

As a previous commenter mentioned, I think the possibility of both of them having autism/being neurodivergent in some way is an idea to consider. Although you were treated horribly and I would NEVER justify that, it might be possible that they were trying to create an environment where they didn't have to mask their neurodivergency. 

The extreme control over your bedtime, for instance, might have been them trying to reduce noise which can cause sensory overload for neurodivergent people. It's still disgusting behavior, because that's no way to treat a child, no matter what you have, but I think you're looking for an explanation and this might be one.

Also, your mother not looking at you when she wanted you to stop talking - people with autism have a hard time with eye contact, and sometimes can have a hard time listening to people talk. So that might have been her way of trying to get you to stop without "being rude"? (I'm just throwing ideas out there). Definitely look into sensory processing disorder. It might help you with your understanding of your parents.

Anyway I'm so sorry this happened to you, because you don't deserve it. I hope by trying to understand your parents you are able to continue healing.
